title: Pre-existing UAF: two tainted if-diamonds sharing one merge block crash lowerControlledRegions (SIGSEGV)
description: ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FINDING (5bl re-review, 2026-06-03), PRE-EXISTING (reproduces on baseline HEAD, NOT a regression from 5bl). Two tainted br-diamonds reconverging on ONE merge block both build BranchRegions with the SAME MergeBB. lowerControlledRegions lowers regions sequentially; the first region's linearization erases the shared merge (ControlledLowering.cpp ~246/172/211), then lowering the second dereferences the freed block -> deterministic SIGSEGV on VALID input (verify-clean), 0 diagnostics. Repro saved at /tmp/shared_merge_diamond_repro.ll (and the t_min.ll in the review output). ROOT CAUSE: matchDiamond/matchSymmetricDiamond (ControlDetection.cpp ~466-527) place NO extra-predecessor constraint on the candidate merge, unlike tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion (the switch path rejects extra/non-arm merge preds, ~787-789), which is why a gated-switch PAIR safely declines but a diamond pair crashes. FIX OPTIONS: (A) mirror the switch extra-predecessor check into matchDiamond/matchSymmetricDiamond (reject a CandMerge whose pred set exceeds the diamond's own {Pred, Arm(s)}); this also naturally rejects the redundant inner-diamond region in a nested-AND. (B) a guard like the 5bl nested-merge guard but keyed on MergeBB-shared-by-2-INDEPENDENT-regions — must EXCLUDE the legitimate nested-AND coordinated pair (region2.Pred == region1.Mid), which shares its merge but lowers correctly (a blanket MergeBB-count>1 decline wrongly rejects lowering_control_angle_nested_and.ll). Needs its own adversarial review. The 5bl nested-merge guard (ControlDetection.cpp end of detectControlRegions) deliberately does NOT cover this (it covers only the Pred==MergeBB nesting the G4 widening newly reaches). NOT blocking 5bl (pre-existing; 5bl does not worsen it).

description:
BUG (confirmed silent miscompile, clang -O1 reachable). A tainted-scrutinee GATED switch whose merge phi collects DISTINCT quantum handles per case (case0 -> qx, case1 -> qy, ...) is silently miscompiled: the result is collapsed to ONE handle and the other-case edges are dropped.

ROOT CAUSE. The merge-phi discriminator (ControlDetection.cpp:663-669) only checks that every incoming is TAINTED — never that they are the SAME base handle, despite the comment at 643-645 asserting "every incoming the same in-place handle". lowerGatedSwitch step-4 (ControlledLowering.cpp:348-358) then RAUWs the whole phi to the FIRST tainted incoming, silently dropping every other-handle edge. The gated path has NO value-mux (unlike the empty-arm/select-chain path's dissolveSelect).

REPRO (clang -O1, llvm@19 19.1.7, libCQPass.so @ b062f2d; /tmp/cqcheck/sw_distinct_q.c): switch on tainted s with case0 r=cq_phi(qx,.1), case1 r=cq_phi(qy,.2), default r=cq_phi(qx,.4); out=cq_phi(r,1.5). Per-arm gates are correct, but the merge phi RAUW-collapses to qx, so downstream cq_phi(r,1.5) -> cqrt_rz_i32(%h1/*qx*/,1.5) runs on qx unconditionally; qy abandoned. When s==1 the program operates on qx not qy. opt -verify CLEAN, exit 0, NO diagnostic.

EMPIRICAL FRAMING (2026-06-03). (1) Legitimate operation (coherent multiplexer over a quantum scrutinee), not malformed. (2) PURE selection of distinct handles already lowers correctly via the empty-arm mux (/tmp/cqcheck/pure_select.c). (3) Surface restriction can't help: clang -O1 gives IDENTICAL IR for switch / if-else-if / in-place-then-select (/tmp/cqcheck/{ifelse_distinct,inplace_then_select}.c). Trigger is the cross-handle MERGE.

RECOMMENDED FIX (re-scoped 2026-06-03 v2, user-chosen = LOWER CORRECTLY, Bennett MUX-EXCH / controlled-SWAP, FREE the sources).

NOTE — supersedes a v1 "XOR-copy + uncompute" plan, which is NOT physical here: copying a superposition (XOR or add) ENTANGLES the source with the result, and uncomputing the source's prep does NOT disentangle it (no-cloning). To MOVE the selected handle's state into the result AND free the source, the primitive is controlled-SWAP (Fredkin) = Bennett's MUX-EXCH "exchange" strategy (docs/bennett-jl-comparison.md lists MUX-EXCH distinct from copy for exactly this).

LOWERING (both-handle / all-tainted-handle merge):
  regOut = cqrt_alloc_<W>(0)
  for each DISTINCT base handle q (grouped by the arm(s) that select it):
      cqrt_cswap([OR of that arm's case eq-flags], regOut, q)   // controlled-SWAP: move q's state into regOut; q -> |0> in that branch
  RAUW merge phi -> regOut; route downstream uses to it.
Per-arm controlled GATES stay as today (applied before the move). MIXED/classical arms: a classical constant has no quantum source to free -> add/sub-seed (reuse dissolveSelect mux.1/WP4); the constant is trivially uncomputable.

NEW RUNTIME PRIMITIVE REQUIRED: cqrt_cswap (Fredkin / controlled-SWAP) + forward/controlled templates. This REVERSES the bd memory tainted-arm-select-mux-no-new-primitive ("no Fredkin needed") — that holds for the KEEP-SOURCES-LIVE select copy (mux.2), NOT for the FREE-THE-SOURCES move here.

HARDER SUB-PART (non-selected-source uncompute): controlled-SWAP frees only the SELECTED source per branch; NON-selected sources retain prepared state entangled with the scrutinee s (garbage that pollutes regOut's measurement). Fully cleaning them is the nontrivial Bennett/QROM-MUX-EXCH uncomputation (reverse each non-selected source's prep in its branch). Real design work — spike it.

SCOPE / STAGING. This has grown from "reuse dissolveSelect" to a FEATURE: (i) cqrt_cswap primitive (runtime + templates), (ii) MUX-EXCH gated lowering + detection routing, (iii) non-selected-source uncompute, plus (0) an IMMEDIATE interim DECLINE (require same-base-handle uniformity -> WP12 'switch under quantum control', over-decline-safe) to close the silent miscompile NOW while the feature is built (mirrors the mux-diag->mux precedent). Recommend splitting into sub-tasks (0)-(iii).

DETECTION. Discriminator at ControlDetection.cpp:663-669 routes a distinct-base-handle merge phi to the MUX-EXCH lowering (resolve each incoming via cq_phi->operand0 to its base; group by arm). UNIFORM-handle merges keep the cheap RAUW (no mux) — do not regress multihandle/shared/emptydefault.

RELATED. The free-vs-keep-live question also applies to the shipped select mux (mux.1/.2): they leave DEAD sources entangled (assumed live). If that is a concern, file a sibling. See docs/bennett-jl-comparison.md (MUX-EXCH/QROM) + bd memory tainted-arm-select-mux-no-new-primitive (now scoped).

REGRESSION: uniform-handle gated fixtures (gated/_shared/_multihandle/_emptydefault) byte-identical (cheap RAUW, no mux). If staged, the interim decline asserts 'switch under quantum control' + CHECK-NOT cqrt_rz{{.*}}controlled. ir-pass-lit green.

title: Phase 4.x — tainted double-phi feeding a rotation silently miscompiles (diamond-form angle merge)
description:
Found by the aht.1/4.3 adversarial review (2026-06-02). A tainted-condition br-DIAMOND whose merge phi is over rotation ANGLES (classical doubles feeding only cq_phi/cq_theta) is mis-lowered by dissolveBranchPhi's reduceClassicalMux path: f64 is a valid data ABI width, so it emits cqrt_alloc_f64 + cq_template_add_f64_hl_controlled (a fake quantum register holding the angle), then the rotation's angle arg becomes an i32 handle instead of a double. Passes opt -verify (silent miscompile).

ROOT CAUSE: WP10/WP16 angle handling fires only for the SELECT form (detection's select branch -> isCleanAngleSelect/AngleSelectRegion). The br-diamond + double-phi form is not routed to angle handling; dissolveBranchPhi treats the classical double phi as integer handle DATA.

REPRO (ir-pass): a tainted icmp -> br i1 -> empty arm -> merge phi double [a,arm],[b,entry] -> cq_phi(u, phi). See /tmp/f5.ll pattern in session.

FIX OPTIONS: (a) SAFE/minimal — in detection, when a matched diamond's merge phi is floating-point + classical, diagnose 'rotation angle under quantum control' (do NOT build the region -> no linearization, no miscompile); mirrors the WP9 B1 diagnostic and the diagnose-first posture. (b) FULL — lower it as controlled-rotation-by-difference (the diamond-phi analog of reduceAngleSelect/WP16). Start with (a).

PRIORITY: silent miscompile (worst class). Adjacent to the aht.3 jump-table guard (commit 859fc50) which restored 'no silent miscompile' for the memory-index path; this is the remaining angle-via-diamond hole.
close_reason:
Fix (a) landed (diagnose-first): detection-time guard unlowerableClassicalMergePhi in ControlDetection.cpp rejects a tainted-condition diamond / gated switch whose merge phi is a wholly-classical non-handle value, on the 'rotation angle under quantum control' surface — never builds the region, no miscompile/broken module.

- Helper mirrors the select-form B1 predicate (!isIntegerTy() || abiWidthFromType().empty()), so it catches f64 (the reported repro) AND, per adversarial review, <2 x double> vectors, i128/odd-width integers, and pointers (a plain isFloatingPointTy() test was strictly weaker). Legitimate i32/i64 classical-data muxes (WP4/WP7) still lower.
- Wired into all FOUR region-building paths: matchDiamond, matchSymmetricDiamond, matchNestedAnd, and tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion (the gated-switch path was a SIBLING hole discovered while verifying — a classical-double switch merge phi left dangling after linearization → 'PHI nodes not grouped' broken module; threaded TaintSet& in to guard it).
- 6 negative lit fixtures, each proven to fail on the unfixed baseline and pass with the fix: lowering_control_angle_diamond{,_sym,_vec,_i128}.ll, lowering_control_angle_nested_and.ll, lowering_control_angle_switch_gated.ll.
- Full suite green (92 ir-pass lit, 11/11 ctest suites incl. frontend + 7 e2e).

Fix (b) — the actual diamond/switch-form angle lowering as controlled-rotation-by-difference — tracked in test_C_libtooling-byx (+ the WP17 source-location polish: point the diagnostic at the consuming rotation, not the phi).

title: Re-sweep: false-successor arm polarity + value-propagated Pred-edge φ
description: Phase 4.3 audit re-sweep finding (pre-existing Phase-4-core silent miscompile + crash). clang canonicalizes if(u!=k)/if(!cond) to an inverted compare with SWAPPED branch targets, putting the single gate arm on the FALSE successor. Two bugs: (1) the control flag was the raw compare with gates fired on flag=1 — the NEGATION of the source condition (silent miscompile); (2) clang value-propagates the merge's straight-through edge to a known CONSTANT (e.g. if(u!=5) → entry edge = 5), so the gate φ RAUW'd to the constant instead of the handle → cq_measure(constant) crash. Fix: matchDiamond reports ArmIsFalse; substituteControlled fires the arm on ¬flag via the cqrt_x bracket when region.ArmNegated; dissolveBranchPhi RAUWs a gate φ to its TAINTED incoming (the handle), not the Pred edge. Compound/nested negated conditions were already correct (clang preserves the real icmp_ne predicate in the && form).

title: Fix opcode_table.yaml fcmp predicate set: one -> une (C != emits une)
description:
The fcmp predicate set in tools/opcode_table.yaml ships 'one' (ordered-not-equal) but Clang emits 'une' (unordered-not-equal) for C '!=' on floats at -O1 (no fast-math). Net effect: a tainted (float != float) lowers to cq_template_fcmp_une_<W>, which DOES NOT EXIST -> link failure; meanwhile the 8 generated _one_ symbols are dead (no -O1 C source emits them).

EVIDENCE (Apple clang 17, -O1 -emit-llvm):
  a == b -> fcmp oeq
  a != b -> fcmp une   <-- yaml has 'one', not 'une'
  a <  b -> fcmp olt
  a >= b -> fcmp oge
Runtime header today: grep -c _one_ = 8, grep -c _une_ = 0.

Accurate C float-comparison predicate set is {oeq, une, olt, ogt, ole, oge}. (ROADMAP's '14 predicates' is also wrong for the same reason — C emits exactly 6, one per operator.)

## Context
Surfaced during Phase 3 design dialogue (full opcode lowering). Predicate-flip canonicalization (Q4) maps une<->une, oeq<->oeq, olt<->ogt, ole<->oge for literal-on-left compares, so une must be present. Related to the Phase 3 opcode-lowering workstream and the eventual Phase 8 ABI freeze.
acceptance_criteria: predicates.fcmp in opcode_table.yaml yields 'une' so a tainted C float '!=' links; runtime/cq_templates.{h,c} regenerated via tools/gen_templates.py with the SHA preamble updated; a hand-written .ll (or e2e) fixture exercises a tainted float != float and FileChecks cq_template_fcmp_une_*. Decide as part of fix whether to also retain 'one' for future -ffast-math support or drop it (currently dead at -O1).

title: ir-pass: dispatch on Tainted set membership, not isa<ConstantInt>

This misses non-constant classical operands — e.g. function args, runtime-loaded values (scanf, globals) — which are also classical and should also dispatch to _hl. The taint set built in step 4 is the right predicate: if an operand is in Tainted it carries a quantum handle (symmetric); otherwise it is classical (use _hl, swap if needed so handle is lhs). Since taint sources are Alloc results and propagation only follows Instructions, a tainted add by construction has at least one tainted operand, so the 'both classical' branch is unreachable. Update step-5 dispatch + add a lit test exercising a non-constant classical operand (function arg).

title: runtime+ir-pass: cq_template_add_i32_hl for handle+literal mixed-operand Q+C add

IR pass dispatches: rhs isa ConstantInt -> _hl variant; rhs is a tainted SSA value -> existing symmetric cq_template_add_i32. title: Pre-existing: dead arm-local cq_phi on a mux base lowers to an unbalanced in-arm controlled Rz
description:
ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW FINDING (u5f review, 2026-06-03), PRE-EXISTING (byte-identical old-vs-new — NOT introduced by u5f's G2/G3 widening). In a distinct-base MUX-EXCH gated switch, a DEAD arm-local cq_phi applied to a mux base q (a gate body in q's selecting arm whose RESULT is not what the mux φ edge carries) is collected into the arm's Gate shadow and lowered by substituteArm to an in-arm cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled(f_q, q, angle). The npu.6/u5f uncompute (emitChainInv) inverts only the UNCONDITIONAL prep chain (2-arg cqrt_ry/cqrt_rz with arg0==q), NOT this 3-arg controlled in-arm Rz — so on the SELECTED path q carries an extra Rz that the cswap moves into regOut (intended for real gate bodies) but if the cq_phi result is DEAD (not the φ-carried value) the Rz is stray, leaving regOut with an uncompensated rotation. G3b (per-arm correspondence) checks that a gate on q lives in a q-SELECTING arm but does NOT check that the gate's result is actually THREADED to the merge φ (vs a dead local). Needs its own adversarial review to (a) confirm reproducibility on a concrete fixture and (b) decide fix: tighten G3b to require the gate body's result reach the mux φ edge (resolveGatedHandleBase of the φ incoming == the gate, not just == its base), OR decline a mux arm containing a dead base-mutating gate. Probe label 'p2' in the u5f review. Over-decline is always safe. See docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md §3 (G3a/G3b) + [[mux-exch-gate-per-arm-correspondence]].

## Context
Surfaced while implementing u5f (G2/G3 multi-op Bennett uncompute). Reviewer classified it pre-existing and out-of-scope for u5f; filed for a future hardening pass, mirroring how the shared-merge UAF (ehf) was split out of 5bl.
notes: RESOLVED — NOT A BUG (investigated 2026-06-03, empirical + independent adversarial verification). The hazard requires NON-LINEAR handle use (a no-cloning violation): a 'dead' cq_phi on mux base q whose result is not threaded to the φ needs q used twice off the same SSA value, which a well-formed linear program (CQ.h frontend; a truly dead/leaked handle is itself a linearity violation) cannot produce. Empirically a non-linear dead-clone arm lowers BYTE-IDENTICALLY to the well-formed linear two-gate arm (in-place handle model RAUWs {q, cq_phi(q,.), .} to one handle, so both cq_phi become two cqrt_rz on the one register = the valid linear interpretation; the 'extra' Rz is only extra under the non-physical cloning reading). The cswap captures all in-arm gates before the move and the non-selected uncompute IS balanced. Adversarial verifier (10 probe categories: linear chains, shared/folded arms, cross-block preps, default/direct-default, chained-theta+gate, measure/return escapes, crash sweep) found ZERO accepted-and-miscompiled inputs; every genuine cross-arm hazard is over-declined by G3b (_wrongarmmut*) and every cross-φ/post-merge cloning hazard by G6 (_crossphi_alias, _postmergelive). NOTE: a general IR-level no-cloning/linearity CHECKER is out of scope by design — the spec §1 establishes correctness by-construction on linear well-formed input, with the frontend guaranteeing linearity and specific cloning shapes declined (G6). Locked the well-formed sibling shape with lowering_control_switch_gated_distinct_multigatearm.ll.

title: Non-selected-source uncompute for MUX-EXCH (Bennett/QROM disentangle)
description: Sub-task (iii) of npu.1, the HARD part flagged 'real design work — spike it'. controlled-SWAP frees only the SELECTED source per branch; NON-selected sources retain prepared state ENTANGLED with the scrutinee s (garbage that pollutes regOut's measurement). Reverse each non-selected source's prep in its branch (Bennett / QROM MUX-EXCH uncomputation). Spike the design first.
acceptance_criteria: MUX-EXCH lowering disentangles non-selected sources so regOut's measurement is correct across all scrutinee values (not just the selected branch); demonstrated end-to-end (clang -O1 -> cq-lowering -> verify) on the distinct-handle multiplexer.
notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-03). PREREQUISITE BLOCKER: uncomputing a source's cq_theta (Ry) prep needs cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv — the runtime has ONLY cqrt_rz_<W>_controlled_inv. Add 7 widths (i1/i8/i16/i32/i64/f32/f64) in runtime/cq_runtime.{h,c} + a ControlledSymbols accessor (mirror controlledRotationFn) FIRST. PLAN (direct-cq_theta case): for each base handle q, uncompute its prep on the branches where q is NON-selected — controlled on ¬f_q (= OR of the OTHER handles' selection flags) — by emitting cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(¬f_q, q, angle). Recover <angle> from the already-lowered cqrt_ry call on q (rotation lowering runs BEFORE controlled lowering, so the cq_theta is gone — scan for the cqrt_ry whose handle is q). GENERAL CASE (the 'spike it' part, UNSOLVED): a source with a multi-op prep history, a chained theta, or live out-of-region uses can't be naively reversed (Bennett/QROM-MUX-EXCH). TIGHTLY GATE: only lower when every base handle is a single direct cqrt_ry prep with no out-of-region uses; else decline (npu.1 path) — over-decline-safe. CANNOT be correctness-validated in the trace-only runtime (structural fixtures only).
GATE SPEC WRITTEN: docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md (adversarial design review 2026-06-03, 6 attackers + synth). REFRAME (confirmed): uncompute correctness is a unitarity theorem (U†U=I) validated by construction + gate-sequence fixtures like every other gate — NOT a simulator gap. The whole risk is the GATE admitting an unsafe case. Spec defines an 8-layer CONSERVATIVE gate G0-G7 (decline on any failure): G0 npu.1 structure/identity; G1 base is a direct cq_theta (not select/phi/arg/data-op); G2 single-Ry (classical arg0, reject chained theta); G3 no extra mutation between prep and merge (reject theta-then-cq_phi Rz garbage); G4 no direct-to-merge default for a distinct-base mux phi; G5 variable-angle dominance; G6 cross-phi base disjointness + region-wide LIVENESS (no-cloning / dead-after-merge — this absorbs the liveness angle); G7 uniform width across mux bases. Plus prerequisites (the 7 cqrt_ry_*_controlled_inv + WidthDispatch resolver + DominatorTree), the ATOMIC-LANDING requirement (gate+mux+uncompute+symbols are one indivisible commit, else revert to the npu.1 decline), the narrow happy-path that lowers, impl order, the positive+decline+regression fixtures, and 4 open risks. See the doc.
close_reason: Non-selected-source uncompute landed atomically with npu.5. Per-non-selected base cqrt_ry_<W>_controlled_inv(NOT f_q,q,angle) (7 ry inverse runtime symbols + ControlledSymbols::controlledRyInvFn). Angle recovered from lowered cqrt_ry (recoverRyAngle); width from taint.HandleWidth. Adversarial review confirmed algebra correct for 2/3/4/5-base; found+fixed C1 (G3b per-arm correspondence silent-miscompile). Spec G3b updated; regression fixtures wrongarmmut{,_default}.

Per-arm controlled gates stay as today (applied before the move). Mixed/classical arms reuse the dissolveSelect add/sub seed. Uniform-handle gated fixtures byte-identical.
notes:
SPIKE FINDINGS (2026-06-03; npu.4 landed cqrt_cswap + ControlledSymbols::cswapFn). IMPLEMENTATION MAP: (1) Detection (tryBuildGatedSwitchRegion, ControlDetection.cpp) currently DECLINES distinct-base φ via the npu.1 same-base-handle check — route those to a MUX-EXCH region instead (new ControlRegion flag + per-φ base-handle→arms grouping). (2) Lowering: replace the step-4 RAUW with: regOut=cqrt_alloc_<W>(0); for each distinct base handle q, f_q = OR of the ArmFlags of the edges selecting q (default edge → ¬OrAll, materialize via a self-inverse cqrt_x bracket like substituteArm's Negate path); emit cqrt_cswap(f_q, regOut, q); RAUW φ→regOut. The MUX-EXCH detection gate (G0-G7) and lowering structure are specified in docs/npu6-mux-exch-gate-spec.md (npu.5+npu.6 must land atomically; npu.5 alone is a silent miscompile). title: Phase 4.1 — gated multi-arm switch/if cascade (general side-effecting arms)
description:
Phase 4.1 follow-on (PRD §8.5, IMPL §13 WP18). The ONE multi-way shape that does NOT fold into the switch→select-chain normalization (-aht.1): a cascade of arms with ARBITRARY SIDE-EFFECTING gate bodies (distinct gate sequences / controlled arithmetic per case, not just a value or a rotation angle). There is no value to select — each arm's ops must become _controlled on its eq-flag.

Mechanism = controlled-region substitution: the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm diamond generalized to an N-way FALSE-arm chain. Compute N mutually-exclusive eq-flags (default = AND of negated flags, Toffoli ladder); control each arm's gates on its flag via LIFO cqrt_x brackets; dissolve φ via WP7's multi-φ path. This is the CQ analog of Bennett.jl's _expand_switches br-cascade — the Option-B fallback.

SEPARATE from -aht.1's select-chain unit (different mechanism — do not conflate). RED: lowering_control_switch_gated.ll (switch(q) whose arms apply distinct gate sequences to an external handle). DONE: gated multi-arm switch lowers to per-arm controlled gates; no residual switch/br i1 on a handle. Depends on u6v.1 (multi-φ dissolution) + u6v.2 (symmetric diamond).
notes:
CLARIFICATION (2026-06-02): this is an IMPLEMENTATION task, NOT a Bennett.jl import and NOT a from-scratch research spike. Bennett is a REFERENCE only — no Julia dependency. The "Option-B fallback" (br-cascade) means a CQ-side C++ desugaring modeled on Bennett's _expand_switches IDEA, reimplemented in our own LLVM pass — never linking or subprocessing Bennett. The mechanism is already chosen: generalize the Phase 4.3 WP8 symmetric two-content-arm controlled substitution to an N-way false-arm chain.

BUT the design is lighter than -aht.1's, so START WITH A DIAGNOSE-FIRST SPIKE: empirically confirm the gated-cascade shape actually survives clang -O1. We have NOT pinned the exact -O1 output the way the Phase 4.3 audit did for the 44 if-shapes; arbitrary side-effecting per-case bodies are *believed* not to fold into selects/angle-selects, but verify before implementing. Only after the shape is pinned, implement the WP8 generalization.

No urgency / no risk while open: the shape is currently SAFE — loud-diagnosed by the WP12 / u6v.6 tainted-switch guard (no silent miscompile).
close_reason: Diagnose-first spike done on real clang -O1 IR: gated cascade survives as a SwitchInst (safe). WP18 implemented — gated multi-arm switch → N-way controlled substitution (per-case eq-flags, default on ¬OR, reuse substituteArm, N-way φ dissolution, linearize). Commit ff13ead. Fixture switch_gated now POSITIVE. Spike also fixed a silent miscompile (jump-table, commit 859fc50). Follow-ons filed: 5zu (jump-table lowering), 509 (default-direct/sparse). title: Diagnose (don't silently miscompile) a tainted-arm select until the mux lands
description:
INTERIM SAFETY NET for the deferred tainted-arm select mux (test_C_libtooling-mux).
Until .1/.2 land, the pass should REJECT the unsupported shape loudly rather than emit
semantically-wrong IR.

BUG: a tainted-condition `select` with >=1 tainted value arm is silently passed through.
detectControlRegions (ControlDetection.cpp ~311) `continue`s past it (no region built),
and because the feeding compare has a select-condition user, isDataPositionCompare also
bails — so the `icmp` is left comparing the RAW qubit handle integer and the select is
left classical. The result links, runs, and measures garbage (a handle id vs a constant)
with NO diagnostic. Every other unsupported shape in the pass emits a loud
DiagnosticInfoUnsupported (diagnoseNoTemplate / RotationLowering::diagnoseUnsupported /
ControlDetection::diagnoseEscape). The select-mux gap has none because the existing
branchEscapes guard only covers br-diamonds, and -O1 turned this `if` into a select (no
br to escape-check).

Repro: example/test_control.c  ->  `if (a>0) b += 12 - a;`  ->
  %2 = select i1 %1, i32 %h_op, i32 -3   (left un-lowered, no diagnostic)

FIX: in detectControlRegions, when a tainted-condition select has >=1 tainted arm and is
NOT a flag-conjunction (matchFlagConjunction already handles the i1-over-flags idiom),
emit DiagnosticInfoUnsupported at the select ("cq controlled lowering: data multiplexer
with quantum arm not yet supported") instead of silently continuing. Mirror the existing
diagnose* surfaces so a fixture can FileCheck it.

SUPERSEDED BY the mux feature: once test_C_libtooling-mux.1 (mixed arm) lands, the
diagnostic narrows to the still-unsupported both-handle case (until .2); once .2 lands it
is removed entirely. Keep the guard scoped so it fires ONLY on the genuinely unsupported
residue, never on a shape a child already lowers.

Cross-ref: PRD §5, IMPLEMENTATION §5.5.
acceptance_criteria: A tainted select with >=1 tainted arm emits DiagnosticInfoUnsupported (DS_Error) at the select instead of passing through; a FileCheck fixture pins the message; classical-arm selects and the shipped WP3-WP6 fixtures stay byte-identical / unaffected.
close_reason: OBSOLETE — superseded by the mux feature (test_C_libtooling-mux .1+.2), per this issue's own 'removed entirely once .2 lands' note. The diag was an INTERIM safety net to diagnose-not-miscompile tainted-arm selects WHILE the mux was deferred. title: Mixed-arm select mux (one classical arm) via the existing HH controlled adder
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, A, B` with the condition tainted and EXACTLY ONE value arm
tainted (a handle); the other arm classical (constant or runtime variable).
Real -O1 of example/test_control.c:
  %1    = icmp sgt i32 %h, -3
  %h_op = cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 9, i32 %h)        ; the tainted true arm (12 - a)
  %2    = select i1 %1, i32 %h_op, i32 -3              ; B = -3 is classical

CONSTRUCTION (mirrors the WP4 classical-arm reduction, PRD §2.6, with HL->HH and a
register delta). Let C be the classical arm, Q the tainted arm; ctrl = flag if Q is the
true (flag=1) arm, else the complemented flag (see below):
  1. delta = Q - C  as a REGISTER, via the existing UNCONTROLLED data template
     cq_template_sub_<W>_hl(Qhandle, Cclassical)  (no controlled form needed here).
  2. regC = cqrt_alloc_<W>(Cclassical)            (seed from the classical arm).
  3. Res  = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(ctrl, regC, delta)   ; the HH controlled add.
     Resolver: ControlledSymbols::controlledDataTemplateFn("add", W, Shape::QQ,
     /*inverse=*/false) -> (flag, handle, handle); name = cq_template_add_<W>_controlled.
  4. RAUW the select to Res; register Res tainted + BirthOrder slot (dissolveSelect
     already does this for the classical/classical path).
Result = C + ctrl·(Q - C) = ctrl ? Q : C. For the example (Q=12-a, C=-3, ctrl=flag):
-3 + flag·((12-a)-(-3)) = flag ? (12-a) : -3. Correct.

CONTROL SENSE: if the CLASSICAL arm is the TRUE arm (select i1 %f, C, Q), seed regC and
control on the complemented flag (cqrt_x(f) bracket, uncomputed LIFO — reuse §2.5
ControlledSymbols::xFn), so result = C + ¬f·(Q-C) = f ? C : Q. (Or equivalently swap and
keep flag — pick one and pin it in the fixture.)

  - The feeding icmp lowers as the control flag exactly as in the WP3/WP4 path
    (ControlFlag); it does NOT go down the data-position CompareLowering path

(unchanged). Phase 4 still brackets only the control flag (+ the ¬f X-bracket when the
classical arm is the true arm).

Audit 2026-06-02: plain 'if(q) return' and measure-in-arm DIAGNOSE cleanly today (good). BUT goto/break out of a tainted arm CRASH instead — -O1 reshapes them into multi-phi diamonds that hit Phase 4.3 Family A (u6v.1) before the escape guard fires. So this refinement now also covers goto/break, and depends on Family A landing (then they either lower or reach the escape diagnostic).
VERDICT FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.6, IMPL §13 WP17): REJECT-by-default is CORRECT and confirmed by the Julia stack + literature — the terminal state, not a stopgap.

- Measurement under quantum control: reject PERMANENTLY. Bennett.jl has no measure op (classical→reversible; measurement lives in Sturm/Orkan); Sturm forbids measure/return inside when(q); Silq's rejected `condMeas` IS this exact program (a measure gated on a superposed predicate is unphysical — you'd have to measure the control first).
- return/break/goto under quantum control: reject by default. Bennett cfg.jl raises a loud error on non-reconverging exits ("lower_loop!: IRRet in loop body … not supported"). Quantum Control Machine (arXiv:2304.15000) proves a superposed jump/return is non-injective and cannot be a unitary; necessary+sufficient = injectivity + synchronization (all branches reconverge). Janus Structured Reversible Program Theorem: banning arbitrary goto/break/return loses NO expressive power — refactor.

-fcq-measurement-bridge: accept ONLY as an explicit opt-in DEMOTION to classical control via deferred measurement — insert the measure AT THE REGION BOUNDARY (collapse predicate before body), loud diagnostic, and STATICALLY REJECT re-entry of the measured value into a still-coherent region (= Silq's sanctioned fix / OpenQASM-3 feed-forward). Sold as a transparent "same if" lowering it is an ANTI-PATTERN (silently changes observable behavior; Silq/Q#/Quipper refuse it).

FUTURE (capture only, not this phase): return/break via DONE-FLAG predication for the BOUNDED + RECONVERGING subset — retval register + done ancilla; write retval & set done on the exit predicate; control every post-exit op on ¬done; final return writes retval on ¬done; UNCOMPUTE done at exit (recompute predicate from live args, CNOT off) or it leaks as garbage entangled with the result. QCM/Tower/if-conversion. True non-reconverging escape stays rejected.

Sturm ships the DUAL — deferred_measurement.jl (measure-then-classical-branch → controlled gate, true=control/false=anti-control, Nielsen-Chuang §4.4) — a collapse-free optimization worth a SEPARATE future pass. The break/goto crash path is already handled by the u6v.8 catch-all diagnostic.

Options: (a) DEFAULT — pre-run stock LLVM -lowerswitch before cq-lowering, folding the switch into icmp-eq chains + selects/brs so it collapses into shapes Phase 4 already handles; (b) native multi-way controlled mux (control on q==0, q==1, ...). Acceptance: a switch(q) program lowers to the expected controlled trace; LIT fixture pins the chosen normalization. Depends on Phase 4 core.
notes:
Audit 2026-06-02 (PRD §7 Family E): the 'pre-run stock -lowerswitch' default is NOT free. -lowerswitch emits a balanced pivot TREE (icmp slt/eq + br with SHARED MULTI-PRED phi-merges); matchDiamond accepts a shared multi-pred merge -> linearization frees a still-referenced block -> CRASH. Surviving switch (no lowerswitch) silently miscompiles (branches on quantum handle id) — now guarded by Phase 4.3 Family D diagnostic (u6v.6). Switch lowering here depends on Phase 4.3 A (u6v.1) + C (u6v.2) landing first AND a NEW closed-diamond guard in matchDiamond (require merge has exactly 2 preds = Pred,Arm); then re-verify the pivot-tree path.
DIRECTION FINALIZED 2026-06-02 (PRD §8.2, IMPL §13 WP15): switch lowering = data-flow SELECT-CHAIN normalization, NOT -lowerswitch. A `normalizeTaintedSwitch` step (between taint-prop and region detection) rewrites a tainted-scrutinee SwitchInst + N-way merge φ into `icmp eq` flags + a nested `select` chain, then the EXISTING dissolveSelect/reduceClassicalMux path lowers it (icmp-eq HL flags + classical-mux/mux.1 controlled adds).

Supersedes Family E ("-lowerswitch + closed-diamond guard"): the select form never produces br-diamonds, so it sidesteps the pivot-tree shared-multi-pred-merge CRASH this issue's own notes found, AND needs no N-way φ dissolution (φ collapses to binary selects) and no new ABI.

Confirmed against Bennett.jl `_expand_switches` (fetched+verified 2026-06-02): same "eliminate switch by reduction" move, but Bennett targets a br-cascade because its downstream is gate-emission-over-CFG; CQ targets selects because downstream is opcode-replacement-over-dataflow. CQ also never inherits Bennett's U11 global-φ-incoming-rewrite trap (we read then DELETE the φ; merge becomes single-pred).

Scope: first cut = value-merge, break-terminated, clean reconverge (merge preds = case/default only). Also covers multi-way value `if` for FREE (PRD §8.3) and angle-switch via angle-select-chain (NEW WP16, generalizes u6v.4/WP10). Gated SIDE-EFFECTING multi-arm cascade is split to a NEW follow-on (different mechanism: controlled substitution / Bennett br-cascade fallback). Gate-level depth opt (unary iteration / QROM, arXiv:1805.03662) is BELOW the cqrt_* ABI = runtime concern, not this issue. Depends: u6v.1 (multi-φ infra) + u6v.4 (angle-select).
close_reason: WP15 (value-merge switch → select-chain via normalizeTaintedSwitch) + §8.3 (multi-way value if for free) + WP16 (angle-select-chain). Commits a69c247, 18027c4. Fixtures: switch_lower, multiway_if, angle_switch (+ angle_chain_nonexcl negative).

title: ir-pass: canonicalize Q+Q operand order by handle creation time
description: clang -O1 canonicalizes commutative add operands by SSA index, so the runtime trace for 'quantum int c = a + b;' depends on which handle was alloc'd first by clang's IR-numbering — currently worked_example traces (h1, h0) and full_example's Q+Q add traces (h4, h3). A future clang version could change this; the e2e harness uses byte-exact diff so we'd get spurious failures. Fix: in step 5 of CQLoweringPass.cpp, track handle creation order via a DenseMap<Value*, unsigned> BirthOrder (Allocs assigned in step 2, cq_template_add_i32 results assigned in step 5). When lowering a Q+Q add (both operands in Tainted), order the call's operands by BirthOrder so the older handle becomes lhs. This restores PLAN.md §4.7.1's canonical (h0, h1) format and makes the trace stable across clang versions. Refresh worked_example and full_example expected.log after landing.

title: Phase 4 prototype: validate region handling (cq_when_*) on stock LLVM
description: Add a fourth pass cq-control that, within cq_when_begin/cq_when_end brackets, substitutes each cqrt_template_* call with its _controlled variant (taking the region's control handle as an additional first argument). Validates that region detection + controlled-variant substitution is implementable on stock LLVM, which is the one architectural mechanism (region handling) the existing Phase 2/5/7 prototypes have not touched.
design: cq-control operates on post-lowering IR (after cq-lowering has dissolved qint_mid_t and emitted cqrt_*). For prototype simplicity, the test input declares cq_when_begin as taking i32 directly (the handle), avoiding the qint_mid_t→handle resolution that real integration would need. Linear CFG only — begin and end in same BB. No nested regions. The mechanism: walk each BB, track 'current control' state, for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region emit a _controlled variant with the control prepended to args, erase brackets at end.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (additions only — existing passes unaffected). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-control runs without crash on hand-written post-lowering input. 3. Output passes opt -verify. 4. cq_when_begin and cq_when_end call sites erased. 5. cqrt_template_add_i32 inside the region is replaced by cqrt_template_add_i32_controlled with the control handle as the first argument. 6. cqrt_template_* calls OUTSIDE any region are NOT substituted (verified by adding a second template call after cq_when_end).
notes: Out of scope for this validation increment: qint_mid_t→handle resolution at cq_when_begin (would be an extension to cq-lowering); cross-BB regions (real cq_when_* can span branches); nested regions (multi-control accumulation); the inverse case cq_invert_begin/_end (separate but similar mechanism reusing emit_inverse from Phase 5). Companion: docs/architecture.md §5.1 + §7.5 (region brackets), docs/backend.md §5.9 (region handling spec).
close_reason: Phase 4 region-handling prototype succeeds. New cq-control pass (~80 LOC) walks each BB tracking cq_when_begin/end bracket state; for each cqrt_template_* call inside a region, substitutes the _controlled variant prepending the control handle. Test verifies: inside-region call replaced, outside-region call preserved, brackets erased, exactly 1 controlled call site + 1 plain call site. Linear single-BB regions only — nested + cross-BB regions deferred but use same stock LLVM API (BasicBlock iteration + IRBuilder + Module.getOrInsertFunction). See prototype/test/input_phase4.ll, run_test_phase4.sh.

title: Phase 5 multi-BB validation increment

design: Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with one cq_init_i32 in entry block, branch to then/else arms that each measure the value, merge block with phi + ret. The handle's post-dominator is the merge block; algorithm should insert there. No code changes to cq_pass.cpp expected — this validates that the existing computeFreePoint() handles the multi-BB case correctly, which is the architecturally-novel question.

Output passes opt -verify. 4. cqrt_free is emitted in the merge basic block (post-dominator of both arms). 5. cqrt_free is NOT emitted in either branch arm. 6. Output has exactly one cqrt_free per handle (no duplication).
notes: Companion: prototype/test/input.ll (linear case), prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh (existing test). New: prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll + prototype/test/run_test_phase5_branch.sh. If the existing pass doesn't handle multi-BB correctly, that's a fix to make — but the design (findNearestCommonDominator + getFirstInsertionPt fallback) should already be correct.
close_reason: Phase 5 multi-BB validation succeeds. Hand-crafted Stage 4 IR with branch (entry → then/else → merge), one cq_init_i32 in entry, measure in both arms. opt-19 -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces exactly one cqrt_free emitted in the merge block (post-dominator) — not duplicated into either arm. PostDominatorTree.findNearestCommonDominator(then, else) correctly returns merge; getFirstInsertionPt() places the free at the right point (between phi and ret). No code changes were needed — existing computeFreePoint() handles multi-BB correctly. See prototype/test/input_phase5_branch.ll, run_test_phase5_branch.sh.

title: Phase 7 prototype: validate call-graph specialization on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a third pass cq-specialize that demonstrates function cloning + call-site retargeting via stock LLVM CloneFunction / CloneFunctionInto + ValueToValueMapTy. For each call site with a qint_mid_t-typed argument, clone the callee, rename to __cq_q_<f>_q1, and retarget the call site. Validates that the Phase 7 mechanism (call-graph specialization synthesis) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use CloneFunction(F, VMap) to clone the callee preserving signature. Set linkage to private/internal so DCE can remove the original if all uses are retargeted. Rename via Function::setName. Walk call sites of the original; for each whose arg is qint_mid_t-typed, replace setCalledFunction to the clone. Minimal scope: signature is preserved, no Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse) — that is downstream implementation that uses the same already-validated emit_inverse mechanism from Phase 5. The point here is to confirm CloneFunction + call-site retargeting compose with the existing cq-lowering pass.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize runs without crash on a test input with one function-call site. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. A new function named __cq_q_<original>_q1 exists in the module. 5. The clone has the same signature as the original (signature rewriting deferred). 6. The original call site is replaced with a call to the clone. 7. Both functions (original + clone) are well-formed.
notes: Out of scope: signature rewriting to (i32, i32) handle ABI, Bennett wrap-around (forward + CNOT-copy + reverse), specialization caching across multiple call sites, recursion handling, q-arg-mask discrimination beyond binary 'has qint_mid_t arg or not'. These are downstream once cloning + retargeting compose with lowering. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 7 prototype validates call-graph specialization. cq-specialize pass uses stock LLVM CloneFunction (+ ValueToValueMapTy) to clone callees with qint_mid_t-typed args, renames via __cq_q_<f>_q1 mangling, retargets call sites. Test: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes=cq-specialize produces a clone with internal linkage that preserves the original function's body shape (extractvalue + add + insertvalue + ret), call site in @example now references the clone, zero remaining calls to the original from @example, output passes opt -verify. See prototype/test/run_test_phase7.sh, prototype/test/output_phase7.ll.

title: Phase 5 prototype: validate auto-uncomputation on stock LLVM
description: Extend the prototype/ pass plugin with a second pass cq-uncompute that demonstrates last-use-driven uncomputation emission via stock LLVM PostDominatorTree analysis. For each handle SSA value (produced by cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 / cqrt_alloc_i32), compute the post-dominating last use and emit cqrt_free(handle) at that point. Skip handles that escape via ReturnInst. Validates that the Phase 5 mechanism (per-op compile-time adjoints at SSA live-range ends) is implementable on stock LLVM with no fork.
design: Use FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy to obtain PostDominatorTreeAnalysis from a Module pass. Use PostDominatorTree::findNearestCommonDominator over user blocks to find the post-dominator BB; within that BB, find the latest user (linear case) and insert after. Emit cqrt_free as a placeholder for the full adjoint gate sequence — the real inverse template is downstream implementation work, not architecture validation. Single test input (same as main prototype) is sufficient: linear control flow exercises the API without needing complex CFG yet.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Pass plugin builds against stock LLVM 19 (no patches). 2. opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' runs without crash on input.ll. 3. Output IR passes opt -verify. 4. Each handle (cqrt_alloc_classical_i32 result, cqrt_alloc_i32 result) has a cqrt_free(handle) call emitted after its last use. 5. Handle SSA values that escape via ret are not freed. 6. Total pass plugin C++ remains focused (no bloat).
notes: Out of scope: real adjoint gate-sequence emission (cqrt_free as placeholder only), loop-aware uncomputation, multi-BB region uncomputation, multi-width. These are downstream once the core analysis-manager wiring is shown to work. Companion: bd memory prototype-validated-no-fork-2026-05-22, docs/llvm-fork-analysis.md §8.2.
close_reason: Phase 5 prototype validates auto-uncomputation. cq-uncompute pass uses stock LLVM PostDominatorTree (via FunctionAnalysisManagerModuleProxy) to compute the post-dominating last use of each handle, emits cqrt_free at that point, skips handles that escape via ret. Test pipeline: opt-19 -load-pass-plugin -passes='cq-lowering,cq-uncompute' produces 3 cqrt_free calls (one per handle), output passes opt -verify, all checks green. See prototype/test/run_test_phase5.sh, prototype/test/output_phase5.ll.

title: Both-arms-handle select mux (alloc-zero + two controlled adds; preserve reused arms)
description:
SHAPE: `select i1 %f, %hp, %hq` — condition tainted and BOTH value arms tainted handles.
The mixed-arm reduction (.1) cannot apply: cqrt_alloc seeds from a CLASSICAL value, and
here neither arm is classical.

CONSTRUCTION (still NO cswap/Fredkin needed — that is only an in-place alternative):
  1. regOut = cqrt_alloc_<W>(0).
  2. cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f,  regOut, hp)     ; regOut += f·hp
  3. cqrt_x(f)                                          ; form ¬f (LIFO-bracketed)
     cq_template_add_<W>_controlled(f, regOut, hq)      ; regOut += ¬f·hq
     cqrt_x(f)                                          ; restore f
  Result = f·hp + ¬f·hq = f ? hp : hq.
Both hp and hq are READ (a_handle/b_handle operands), never consumed -> PRESERVED for
their other uses. This is the load-bearing difference from .1: an arm here may be live
elsewhere in the function, so a consuming/in-place strategy is unsafe; the additive
copy into a fresh ancilla preserves them.

PASS TOUCH-POINTS: extend the .1 detection gate to ALSO accept both-tainted; add the
both-tainted branch in dissolveSelect emitting alloc(0) + the two controlled adds + the
¬f cqrt_x bracket (reuse ControlledSymbols::xFn and the §2.5 De Morgan LIFO uncompute
discipline). Depends on .1 (shares the detection + dissolution seam).

UNCOMPUTE: regOut is the result (kept); the ¬f X-bracket is uncomputed in place; hp/hq
and any inputs are data temporaries left for Phase 5. Phase 4 brackets the control flag
+ the ¬f X-bracket only.

PRIORITY: lower than .1 — rarer shape (both branch values quantum); .1 covers the
common case. RED fixture: lowering_control_mux_handles_i32.ll; e2e slice modeled on
e2e-slice-control-merge.

NOTE: if a future need wants in-place routing instead of additive copy, cqrt_cswap /
Fredkin (+ controlled/inverse) is the alternative primitive — but it is NOT required to
land this issue.
acceptance_criteria: A 'y=(q>0)?f(q):g(q)' program lowers to cqrt_alloc(0) + two cq_template_add_*_controlled with an uncomputed ¬f cqrt_x bracket; both source handles still referenced afterward; LIT + e2e green; opt -verify clean.
close_reason: Both-arms-handle select mux implemented (gate accepts both-tainted; dissolveSelect alloc(0)+two QQ controlled adds+¬f cqrt_x bracket; arms preserved). LIT+e2e green; opt -verify clean; WP3-WP6 + mux.1 byte-identical. Reviewer ACCEPT.

title: Build -O-level regression matrix for stage-1 clang flag
description: Build a regression test matrix that lets the stage-1 clang -O level be raised above the validated -O1 floor with confidence. Per docs/frontend.md §8 'Optimization-level guidance', stage 1 is currently pinned at -O1 because higher levels introduce risks (aggressive inline pre-empting clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion rewriting signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops; SimplifyCFG flattening branches the post-dom walk depends on; GVN CSE across tainted values; SLPVectorize fusing tainted+untainted scalars into a vector op at -O3). Matrix: small CQ programs compiled at -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3 (each), lowered IR diffed across levels, runtime gate sequences captured and compared. Goal: identify which risks fire in practice, which are theoretical, and whether the stage-1 default can move from -O1 to -O2/-O3 unconditionally or with specific -fno-* flags. Related: 5kb.
notes:

FINDINGS: -O0 correctly REJECTED by the pass (no mem2reg => taint stuck in allocas; floor confirmed from below). -O1==-O2==-O3 BYTE-IDENTICAL gate traces for all 6 probes — none of the frontend.md §8 risks fires. title: Investigate -O2/-O3 viability at stage 1 (post-rest)
description: Currently the pipeline pins clang -O1 at stage 1 (pre-IR-pass). -O1 is the validated floor — minimum needed for mem2reg/SROA cleanup. Higher levels are not prohibited by the design but introduce risks that need a test matrix. Defer until the rest of the taint-driven pipeline transition (frontend.md/backend.md/quantum-classical-handling.md/example.md/ROADMAP) is done.
notes: Stage 1 risks at -O2+: aggressive inline pre-empts clone-on-taint; IPSCCP/argpromotion can rewrite signatures; LoopUnroll/LoopVectorize on tainted loops/conditions; SimplifyCFG flattens branches the post-dom analysis walks; GVN CSE across tainted values. Stage 1 risks at -O3: SLPVectorize can fuse tainted + untainted scalar ops into a single vector op — would silently miscompile without vector-tainted-op template support. Stage 3 (post-pass codegen): any -O level safe — only stock LLVM ops + opaque cqrt_* externals remain; this is where most binary runtime perf comes from anyway. Recommendation: default -O1 stage 1, allow -O3 stage 3, require -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize if user pushes -O3 to stage 1 until vector-tainted templates exist. Need: regression test matrix (small CQ programs compiled at each -O level, lowered IR diffed, runtime gate sequences compared).
